eras.-100: New since the camp, rows of small wooden barracks and gabled houses in red, yellow and grey now stand across the mid-ground on wooden posts, with gravel tracks and tall cable trestles climbing the lower slope of the same mountain. eras.-100: Since the tent camp, a compact coal hamlet now lines the lower slope on the same footprint: two- to three-storey stone barracks painted red, yellow and grey with a small arched market hall bearing Latin tablets, linked by a straight stone-paved track with side drains and a stone-railed wagonway for coal tubs.
